The decision discusses the principle of piercing the corporate veil in the context of arbitral award execution, exploring when courts may disregard separate legal personality to ensure enforcement against parent companies or related entities. The ruling provides clarity on the relationship between arbitration law and corporate law principles, determining the extent to which traditional corporate law doctrines apply in the specialized context of enforcing international arbitral awards. legal.headline: Practising law and pursuing 3-year LLM course simultaneously? Delhi HC lets attendance shortfall slide
legal.hook: The Court observed that “the very purpose of the LLM 3-year course is to enable students to continue practice before the Courts while simultaneously pursuing their Masters program”
legal.summary: The Delhi High Court has permitted a law student to pursue a 3-year LLM course while simultaneously practising law, despite falling short of the mandatory attendance requirements. The Court rejected strict application of attendance rules, observing that the very purpose of the 3-year LLM programme is to enable students to continue practice before courts while pursuing their Master's degree. The judgment recognizes the practical reality that full-time practice and full-time academic attendance are inherently incompatible. Rather than impose a blanket attendance threshold, the Court exercised discretion to allow the student to proceed, emphasizing that the curriculum is designed with working lawyers in mind. The order suggests courts will not mechanically enforce attendance norms when they conflict with the stated pedagogical intent of allowing practitioners to upskill simultaneously.
legal.contextNote: This judgment clarifies regulatory interpretation of Bar Council of India (BCI) rules governing professional qualification requirements for practising advocates. The 3-year LLM is a post-graduation qualification that many in-practice lawyers pursue for specialization (corporate, constitutional, tax law, etc.). The tension between mandatory attendance and working practice creates a recurring compliance friction. This ruling establishes judicial deference to the curriculum's stated dual-track purpose rather than rigid procedural gatekeeping. For lawyers advising educational institutions, bar associations, or individual practitioners: this signals courts will adopt purposive interpretation of attendance rules when the qualification itself contemplates concurrent practice. Panelists concluded that malls will remain commercially relevant over the next two decades, but only by fundamentally transforming their business model. Rather than competing primarily on retail shopping volume, malls must evolve into experience-led, mixed-use, and community-focused ecosystems. This shift emphasizes engagement and experiential offerings alongside traditional retail, suggesting that mall operators must diversify revenue streams and reposition their properties as social and entertainment destinations to remain viable in a landscape likely disrupted by e-commerce and changing consumer behavior.
retail.contextNote: Indian retail real estate faces structural headwinds from e-commerce penetration (Flipkart, Amazon, Jio Commerce expansion) and changing post-pandemic consumer habits.
